title: T1090.004 — Proxy - Domain Fronting
subtitle: Watch the trick in eight steps.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Setting the stage
steps.caption: The attacker registers an app behind a popular CDN. The app shares the CDN’s trusted name and IP space. A hidden zone inside the app points to the attacker’s server.
steps.defender: your allowlist already trusts this CDN, so nothing looks wrong yet.

steps.title: Crafting the trick
steps.caption: The attacker configures the implant with two names. The TLS SNI value names the trusted CDN. The HTTP Host header names the hidden zone on the same CDN.
steps.defender: only a tool that reads inside TLS can ever see both names.

steps.title: The blind pass
steps.caption: The implant connects to the CDN through your firewall. The firewall sees the clear SNI value and it is trusted, so the session passes.
steps.defender: sensors see “trusted CDN, port 443”. This is the blind spot.

steps.title: The relay inside
steps.caption: The CDN edge removes the TLS layer. It reads the Host header and forwards the request to the attacker’s server. The CDN becomes an unwilling relay.
steps.defender: none of this crosses your network, so your logs stay empty.

steps.title: Beacon complete
steps.caption: Commands come back through the same path. Stolen data goes out as small, regular HTTPS uploads.
steps.defender: logs show only harmless-looking CDN traffic with a steady rhythm.

steps.title: Blank-SNI variant
steps.caption: The attacker switches to “domainless” fronting. The implant sends TLS with an empty SNI field but keeps the Host header. Some CDNs still route it.
steps.defender: there is no clear name left to judge, so name-based rules go quiet.

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Turning on the light
steps.caption: The SOC deploys TLS inspection at the web proxy. A rule now compares SNI and Host on every session. It fires on the mismatch and also flags sessions with an empty SNI.
steps.defender: the two names finally meet, and they do not match.

fields.detail: The SOC deploys TLS inspection at the web proxy. A rule now compares SNI and Host on every session.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: Response and adaptation
steps.caption: The analyst blocks the hidden zone at the CDN vendor and at your proxy. A hunt finds two more infected hosts. The rules are generic, so they keep working when the attacker moves to a new provider.
steps.defender: detect the shape, not the brand.
